This SOP describes the end-to-end control flow for an outward telegraphic transfer (OTT), using UOB Singapore public materials as
the UOB-specific baseline and standard cross-border payment practices as the operating framework. UOB publicly identifies
Telegraphic Transfer as a cross-border payment service and states that instructions may be submitted via UOB Infinity or
host-to-host services, while manual TT forms may be submitted at a UOB branch. UOB also provides public guidance on required

clearing codes, additional payment details, payment purpose, cut-off times, value dates, charges, and post-processing tracking.
UOB public UOB states that electronic TT instructions can be submitted via UOB Infinity or host-to-host, and manual applications can be
submitted at branches; MT103 copies can be retrieved via UOB Infinity after processing. [1]
Industry / regulatory Cross-border wire processing should preserve sufficient ordering-party and beneficiary data, provide traceability, and
support monitoring, rejection, repair and investigation. FATF Recommendation 16 is the international reference point for payment
transparency. [13]

3.1 Scope
This SOP covers outward cross-border payment instructions originating from an account at UOB Singapore and intended for a
beneficiary outside Singapore, where the payment is processed as a Telegraphic Transfer. It includes both electronic initiation (e.g.,

OTT passes through: payment operations review, compliance controls, FX/funding, correspondent/agent routing, message

transmission, beneficiary-bank processing, status tracking, exceptions and reconciliation.

[ ] Trade finance instruments such as documentary credits, collections or banker’s guarantees.

[ ] Country-specific legal advice for every destination country.

1. Executive Summary
This SOP describes the end-to-end control flow for an outward telegraphic transfer (OTT), using UOB Singapore public materials as
the UOB-specific baseline and standard cross-border payment practices as the operating framework. UOB publicly identifies
Telegraphic Transfer as a cross-border payment service and states that instructions may be submitted via UOB Infinity or
host-to-host services, while manual TT forms may be submitted at a UOB branch. UOB also provides public guidance on required

clearing codes, additional payment details, payment purpose, cut-off times, value dates, charges, and post-processing tracking.
UOB public UOB states that electronic TT instructions can be submitted via UOB Infinity or host-to-host, and manual applications can be
submitted at branches; MT103 copies can be retrieved via UOB Infinity after processing. [1]
Industry / regulatory Cross-border wire processing should preserve sufficient ordering-party and beneficiary data, provide traceability, and
support monitoring, rejection, repair and investigation. FATF Recommendation 16 is the international reference point for payment
transparency. [13]
The SOP is organized as a control chain rather than a customer click-by-click guide:

[ ] Initiate - capture the instruction from an authenticated channel or accepted physical form.
[ ] Validate - verify required fields, account, currency, amount, destination, beneficiary-bank identifiers, clearing details and purpose.
[ ] Screen and assess - perform customer/instruction screening and risk-based review before release.
[ ] Fund and price - confirm available funds, exchange rate treatment and charge instruction (BEN/SHA/OUR).
[ ] Approve and release - apply the customer mandate and bank controls, then construct and transmit the payment message.
[ ] Route and settle - use the appropriate correspondent / agent path and monitor payment status.
[ ] Confirm and reconcile - reconcile debits, charges, transaction references, payment status and return / exception outcomes.

The key operating principle is that the payment instruction is treated as a controlled data object whose critical data must remain
accurate and traceable from customer initiation through final credit or return.
